notes:
Inbound from small retail brand focused on outdoor gear. Self-serve sign-up on hosted API, used free credits to run embeddings + generation tests. Primary interest: product Q&A widget on product pages + automated short product descriptions for new SKUs. Catalog size ~12k SKUs, seasonal bursts (promo days) with short windows of very high traffic (10x baseline).

Key quotes / call snippets:
- Founder: "We need answers that are accurate to product specs — false positives are worse than silence."
- Ops: "Can we failover to a cheaper model during peaks? Cost spikes are a real concern."

Requirements / preferences (captured during call):
- Workloads: mostly product Q&A (low-latency reads), catalog enrichment (batch/async embeddings), occasional rerank for internal search.
- Latency targets: P50 < 250ms for Q&A, P95 < 600ms preferred.
- Throughput: baseline ~5-10 QPS for widget, burst up to 80-120 QPS during promotions; embedding jobs run in off-peak but need cost predictability.
- Model preference: open / small-to-medium models for cost control; want option to route to higher-capacity model for complex queries.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to cheaper model or cached responses during heavy load.
- Security: SMB but needs SSO for admin console, audit logs for content changes; not strict SOC2 requirement yet.

POC notes & next steps:
- Send tailored pricing that highlights per-token & embedding pool examples and a simple cost projection for a 12k SKU catalog and promo-day burst. (Action: Maya)
- Share hosted API quickstart PDF + sample cURL snippets for product Q&A + embeddings. (Done: quickstart link attached)
- Offer 30m session with SE (Leo) to walk through request routing and batching tips to hit latency targets. Proposed times: next week mornings PST.
- Ask engineering to provide a small anonymized SKUs dump (CSV) so we can run an optimized embedding profile and suggest batching/quantization settings.

Open blockers: budget sign-off, need to confirm token retention/retention_controls for product data (ops question), and a short PCI/data handling clarification from security.
